title: Token-level Cost Attribution Canvas + CSV Export Patterns
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Design an end-to-end UX for token-level cost analytics in the Redwood Console that supports detailed cost breakdown, attribution by route/model/user, CSV export for finance teams, and new pricing UI patterns for presenting per-token vs. per-request tiers. Deliverables: 1) Canvas-level spec showing data flows and attribution granularity options (request, routing rule, model, session); 2) Hi-fi prototype of the Cost > Token view (breakdown + top callers + drilldown panels); 3) Export schema and CSV samples + import notes for finance; 4) Pattern library entries for pricing UI (multi-rate rows, tiered vs. continuous pricing sliders, explanatory microcopy). Constraints: backend can emit per-token attribution aggregated at route+model+customer_tag granularity for time windows >= 1m; real-time streaming attribution is out of scope for this cycle. Accessibility and localization guidelines should be included in the spec. This ticket covers UI decisions and prototypes; implementation tasks will be split to ENG tickets after design sign-off.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable prototype for Desktop showing: overview -> model breakdown -> route attribution -> CSV export flow
CSV export spec documented in Confluence with sample files and column mapping
Pricing patterns documented with examples for two common customer personas (startup usage-focused, enterprise committed-capacity)
PM + Engineering sign-off recorded in PRD and Slack thread
Edge cases and fallback copy defined for partial attribution and missing metadata
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Chen: Created ticket after stakeholder kickoff. Notes from meeting: Finance wants a CSV with columns for date, customer_id, route, model_variant, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, token_cost_usd, billing_metric_id. PM asked for top-20 callers widget.

2026-02-28 Owen Patel: Ran a 2-hour design spike exploring two primary UX approaches — 'stacked waterfall' breakdown vs 'table-first with quick cards'. Preference for cards + interactive table to support export-first workflows.

2026-03-03 Leila Ahmed (PM): PM feedback — prioritize ability to filter by commit/rollout and to attribute costs to rollout variants. Also callout: must show estimated vs actual cost delta when quantization/ batching recommendations are applied.

2026-03-05 Alex Rivera (Eng): Engineering note — backend will provide hourly aggregates and per-request metadata in the next runtime-1.20 telemetry job. We cannot support sub-minute attribution or per-function-call tagging yet. Will open ENG-4682 to surface billing tags to the console API.

2026-03-08 Maya Chen: Uploaded initial hi-fi prototype to Drive: https://drive.redwood.company/design/token-attrib-proto-v1 and Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/COST/Token+Attribution+Spec. Included CSV example files: token-attrib-sample-1.csv, token-attrib-sample-2.csv.

2026-03-10 Usability test (internal, n=6) summary: users found the top-callers card most useful; confusion around 'attribution window' language — changed to 'billing window (UTC)'. Finance asked for a 'rollup by legal entity' option — added to filters.

2026-03-12 Design review with PM/Eng: Approved visual patterns. Decisions made: 1) default export schema uses snake_case column names; 2) show both per-token and per-request columns when pricing tier applies; 3) pricing pattern 'tiered band rows' chosen over continuous slider for clarity in invoices.

2026-03-14 Owen Patel: Updated prototype with accessibility contrast fixes and added keyboard focusflow. Pushed updated images to Drive and linked a short Loom walkthrough in the PRD. Next: final sign-off and handoff to ENG for implementation grooming.
notes: CSV schema: date_utc, customer_legal_entity, customer_id, route, model_variant, session_id, request_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, token_cost_usd, currency, pricing_tier_id. Pricing pattern doc includes invoice-ready rendering mockups and recommended microcopy for invoices and help center entries.
